description: The maintainer's adjacency ruling on issue #944's sibling question: a newline separates exactly like a space -- always, everywhere. Adjacency is whitespace-agnostic; a newline is insignificant to the GRAMMAR, not invisible to the LEXER, and it is now written down normatively at `spec/grammar.md:248`. This is a NARROWING, and the mechanism is why it was invisible: a newline token's `end` IS the next line's column 1, so once a container skipped the newline the following `[` tested as adjacent to what preceded it -- a skipped newline MANUFACTURED an adjacency the source never had. THIS FIXTURE IS A REGRESSION GUARD, NOT A WITNESS, and saying so is the correction of a false claim this description previously carried. Measured against a parser built at `0277d5ff` before the fix, the list literal ALREADY agreed: `[ :nums` + newline + `[1] ]` and `[ :nums [1] ]` both printed `[[10 20 30] [1]]`, and only the GLUED `[ :nums[1] ]` printed `[10]`. The container that actually exhibited the defect was the parenthesized group, and it exhibited it only in the AST -- at that tip both of its spellings raised the same two diagnostics -- so no fixture can witness this fix, because an execution fixture compares printed values and a check fixture compares diagnostics. That witness is the parse-shape comparison in `packages/parser/src/newline-continuations-and-delimiters.test.mjs`. What this fixture pins is that the agreement holds as a VALUE and keeps holding, which is why a list literal is the container: both spellings execute in it. The parenthesized container is malformed in BOTH spellings, so its agreement is pinned in the companion `core-language/check/a-newline-separates-like-a-space-when-malformed`; the top level is excluded from both, because its spaced spelling raises `ol-bad-token` at PARSE stage -- so `check()` never runs -- and its newline spelling is two statements; neither is about adjacency, and statement delimitation is issue #983's subject rather than this slice's. The glued spelling is printed too and must NOT match the other two: without it this fixture would still pass if adjacency stopped working altogether, since all three spellings would then agree on the non-selector reading. The final row is the one-line comprehension, which still maps rather than indexing `:nums`; its SPLIT form is a parse error and so lives in the check twin.
